Definition: probably by contraction for Παρμενίδης (a derivative of a compound of G3844 and G3306); constant; Parmenas, a Christian:--Parmenas.
BiblicalUsage: Parmenas is one of the seven chosen in Acts 6:5, when the church at Jerusalem picks seven men of honest report, full of the Holy Ghost and wisdom, to serve the tables so the apostles can give themselves to prayer and the ministry of the word. He is named with Stephen and Philip, and his service at the tables is the whole of the story Scripture tells of him.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the men who served tables were chosen with the same care as the men who preached, because in the church no work is small when it frees the word to go out.
